takeaway: Acute appendicitis: anorexia, abdominal pain that settles in the right lower quadrant, vomiting, low-grade fever, and lower abdominal and rectal tenderness.

question.text: A 25-year-old woman has 24 hours of anorexia, abdominal pain and diarrhoea. She has vomited and has a low-grade fever. She is tender in the lower abdomen and on rectal exam. Diagnosis?
question.say: A twenty-five-year-old woman has had anorexia, abdominal pain and diarrhoea for twenty-four hours. She has vomited and has a low-grade fever. She is tender in the lower abdomen and on rectal examination. What is the likely diagnosis?

lines.say: This twenty-five-year-old woman has been unwell for twenty-four hours.
She cannot face her lunch. Anorexia is an early clue.
The thermometer shows a low-grade fever.

lines.text: Pain starts generalized, then moves to the right lower quadrant.
lines.say: Her pain began everywhere, then settled low on the right, at McBurney's point.
(sigh) Here is the reason. The appendix is acutely inflamed and very angry, and it is tender on rectal examination too.

lines.text: Remember: anorexia, fever and lower abdominal tenderness mean acute appendicitis.
lines.say: Remember: anorexia, vomiting, low fever and lower abdominal tenderness mean acute appendicitis.
